title: How do you write a number in expanded form?
description: Farhan counts visitors at a village fair. The video writes two numbers in expanded form by adding the value of each digit and leaving out the zeros.
teaching_notes: One idea: expanded form adds the value of each digit, and a zero adds nothing. Watch for the digit next to a zero being read as if it were in the tens place.

video_script.why: The child reads place value but has not yet turned a number into a sum of the value of each digit.
video_script.substitution: Write the value of each digit, add them, and leave out each zero.
video_script.anchor: Farhan counting visitors at the village fair
video_script.wrong_answer: six thousand plus five hundred plus eighty
video_script.wrong_move: Chintu reads the eight as eighty because it is next to a zero. The eight is in the ones place, so it is worth eight.
video_script.payoff_line: a zero adds nothing, so we leave it out

final_answer.spoken: six thousand plus five hundred plus eight, and forty thousand plus one thousand plus two hundred plus thirty

maths_rules: slip: reading the 8 as 80 gives 6,000 + 500 + 80 = 6,580, not 6,508
video_script.design: One idea: expanded form adds the value of each digit and drops zeros. Wrong idea: reading the digit by the zero beside it. Place boxes with values stay on the stage.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='fair'/>Farhan counts visitors at the village fair. One day has six thousand, five hundred and eight visitors. The whole fair has forty-one thousand, two hundred and thirty.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Write each number in expanded form. Expanded form means adding up the value of each digit.

marks.stop: the anchor is underlined in the accent colour

narration: <bookmark mark='stop'/>Stop the video. Say your answer out loud.

narration: <bookmark mark='pv'/>Look at six thousand, five hundred and eight. The six is in the thousands place, so it is worth six thousand.
<bookmark mark='five'/>The five is in the hundreds place, so it is worth five hundred.
<bookmark mark='zero'/>The zero is in the tens place, so it is worth zero. The eight is in the ones place, so it is worth eight.

beats.on_screen: Chintu's bubble shows 6,000 + 500 + 80; the 8 is circled in the ones box; the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

marks.slip: the 8 is circled in the ones box
marks.strike: the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

narration: [chintu] <bookmark mark='chintu'/>Six thousand plus five hundred plus eighty.
<bookmark mark='slip'/>The eight is in the ones place, not in the tens place.
<bookmark mark='strike'/>It is worth eight, not eighty.

beats.on_screen: the values 6,000, 500, 0 and 8 in a row with plus signs; the 0 fades out; the answer 6,000 + 500 + 8 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='add'/>Add the value of each digit. Write six thousand plus five hundred plus zero plus eight.
<bookmark mark='pay'/>A zero adds nothing, so we leave it out.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>That makes six thousand, five hundred and eight equal to six thousand plus five hundred plus eight.

beats.on_screen: 41,230 in place boxes with the values 40,000, 1,000, 200 and 30; the 0 fades out; the answer 40,000 + 1,000 + 200 + 30 is written

marks.split: the values 40,000, 1,000, 200 and 30 appear under the digits
marks.zero: the 0 in the ones box fades out

narration: <bookmark mark='big'/>Next, take forty-one thousand, two hundred and thirty.
<bookmark mark='split'/>The four is worth forty thousand, and the one is worth one thousand. The two is worth two hundred, and the three is worth thirty.
<bookmark mark='zero'/>The zero in the ones place adds nothing, so we leave it out.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>Forty-one thousand, two hundred and thirty is forty thousand plus one thousand plus two hundred plus thirty.
